Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Consistent assessment findings from transcript and DDx:
  - Suspected chest infection / community-acquired pneumonia given fever, acute shortness of breath, pleuritic right-sided back pain on deep inspiration, and reported hemoptysis
  - Differential considerations discussed with DDx support: pulmonary embolism; methotrexate-induced pneumonitis; SLE-related serositis
  - Noted stability on tele-visit (no acute instability evident), but in-person evaluation needed to finalize assessment
- Plan aligned with DDx considerations:
  - In-person clinic today for chest auscultation and vital signs (blood pressure, temperature) and formal exam
  - Consider chest X-ray if symptoms persist or exam findings suggest pneumonia
  - Antibiotics may be indicated if chest infection confirmed; no antibiotic prescribed at this tele-visit pending clinical assessment
  - No active smoking; lives alone; cat exposure noted
  - No known drug allergies
  - No long-haul flight history; family/clot history not clearly documented via tele-visit
  - Plan to book face-to-face assessment with GP today

- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded
  - Arrange same-day in-person evaluation with chest examination and vital signs
  - If pneumonia suspected on exam, initiate appropriate antibiotic therapy per in-person assessment
  - Obtain chest X-ray if symptoms persist or worsen or if exam findings warrant further evaluation
  - Monitor for red flags: escalating shortness of breath, chest pain with deep inspiration, persistent fever, or hemoptysis
  - Return precautions and follow-up scheduling discussed; note left for clinic booking

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Community-acquired pneumonia / chest infection
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Fever, acute SOB, pleuritic pain with deep inspiration, and reported hemoptysis; clinician planned in-person assessment and likely antibiotics if infection confirmed
- Pulmonary embolism
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Acute SOB with pleuritic pain and hemoptysis; SLE increases thrombotic risk; stability noted but imaging/risk assessment needed
- Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: SLE patient on methotrexate presenting with SOB and fever; timing relative to MTX dose exists (last dose this morning)
- (Not expanded here due to 2–3-diagnosis limit; other DDx such as SLE serositis and lung cancer were considered in discussion but not prioritized as top 2–3)
